cards.explanation: The answer is the great King. The song calls Mount Zion "…the city of the great King." That's the title that tells you whose city this is, friends. I put my name on my bakery door, and the song puts the King's title right on Zion.
The answer is False. The song says, "God is in her citadels; He has shown Himself to be a fortress." The fortress isn't a wall or an army, friends. It's God Himself.

The answer is fled. The song says, "They saw and were astounded; they fled in terror." Picture a whole group of kings who showed up together, took one look and ran the other way. That is a short visit, friends.

The answer is a wind from the east. The song tells God, "With a wind from the east You wrecked the ships of Tarshish." Notice the song says it straight to Him, friends. One wind, and those ships were wrecked.
The answer is that they have seen it for themselves. The song says, "As we have heard, so we have seen in the city of the LORD of Hosts…" What they heard matches what they saw, friends.

The answer is True. The song says, "God will establish her forever." The word is forever, friends, and the song doesn't put an end date on it. Right after that comes the word Selah, and I'll leave it right there in the song where it belongs.

The answer is False. The song says, "Within Your temple, O God, we contemplate Your loving devotion." So in the temple they're thinking about His loving devotion, not His power, friends. After kings running and ships wrecked, the song gets quiet and tender.
The answer is to the ends of the earth. The song says, "Your name, O God, like Your praise, reaches to the ends of the earth…" That's about as far as far gets, friends.

The answer is God's judgments. The song says, "Mount Zion is glad, the daughters of Judah rejoice, on account of Your judgments." So the gladness comes on account of His judgments, friends. Gladness and judgments in the same breath, and the song doesn't blink.

The answer is so you can tell the next generation. The song says to tour it all "…that you may tell the next generation." The walk has a purpose, friends, and the purpose is telling. That's like me walking through a recipe step by step so I have something to tell the next baker.

The answer is True. The last line says, "He will be our guide even till death." Notice the song doesn't stop at "…forever and ever…" It also says He guides all the way through life, friends. That's a very good ending.
